date_note: Reuters (relayed by WKZO) is dated Tokyo, Friday 27 November, and was posted 26 November US time; the page gives no earlier day for the speech.
exec: A Bank of Japan executive director says AI's growing ability to find and exploit vulnerabilities adds cybersecurity risks that authorities and institutions must address.
geo_basis: Bank of Japan headquarters, Tokyo; the speech was at an IMF seminar in Tokyo per the report
plain: A Bank of Japan official told a Tokyo seminar that AI's growing ability to find and exploit weaknesses adds cyber risk for new digital money and payment systems, and that security must be built in from the start.

sources.name: WKZO (Reuters), BOJ calls for safeguards against digital money, AI risks
Crypto Briefing, Bank of Japan flags emerging cyber threats to digital money from AI

summary: According to Reuters, as relayed by WKZO, Bank of Japan Executive Director Kazushige Kamiyama told an IMF seminar on digital money and payments in Tokyo that AI's growing ability to find and exploit vulnerabilities adds cybersecurity risks that authorities and institutions must address. He said tokenization could let cyber incidents spread quickly across interconnected platforms, so new platforms need security and resilience built in from the start.
title: Bank of Japan official says AI adds cyber risks to digital money and payment systems

validation.note: Reuters via WKZO and Crypto Briefing read; both relay one speech and are counted as one. The BOJ's own text of the speech was not read.
